title: Stravito shares a financial-services AI persona case study
summary: Stravito describes how a financial-services organization uses AI personas to keep customer perspectives available to its teams. The case study explains the role of existing research and validation in the rollout.

title: Articos compares research for measuring and explaining
summary: Articos separates questions about scale from questions about motivation. Its guide compares qualitative and quantitative methods and considers how synthetic research fits into that choice.

title: Articos explains how to combine findings without losing context
summary: Articos outlines a process for moving from individual responses to shared themes and conclusions. It also discusses where AI can assist with the mechanical work of organizing research.

title: Simile sets out its approach to testing what-if decisions
summary: Simile explains how interviews, surveys and behavioral records can contribute different pieces to a simulation. The article focuses on using those models to explore decisions before taking action.

title: Stravito offers five starting points for using AI personas
summary: Stravito brings together practical advice for moving from persona exploration into business decisions. The article focuses on getting started with clear use cases and connecting the work to an organization's research.

title: Articos updates its guide to evaluating synthetic users
summary: Articos explains how AI-generated participants are built and used for early product questions. The guide discusses validation and the different demands of exploring an idea and confirming a decision.

title: Electric Twin explores audience testing for media teams
summary: Using media examples, Electric Twin describes how simulated subscribers and prospective readers can react to content ideas. The focus is on differences between audiences, rather than one average response.

title: Electric Twin maps synthetic research into the research workflow
summary: Electric Twin compares synthetic studies with conventional fieldwork and explains where each enters a project. Its guide also looks at the data needed to distinguish one customer segment from another.

title: Respondents, personas or panels? Electric Twin unpacks the terms
summary: Electric Twin explains the different products sold under the synthetic-research label. It highlights why a buyer needs to understand the audience data and checks behind a tool, not just its interface.

title: Subconscious describes shelf simulations for retailer discussions
summary: Subconscious looks at comparing shelf arrangements before a retailer meeting. It distinguishes a convincing virtual aisle from a study that actually tests how product choices change.

title: Subconscious explores testing ambassador choices before a deal
summary: Subconscious proposes comparing the attributes of potential brand ambassadors before committing to a contract. It focuses on audience reactions to the specific match between a person, brand and message.

title: Subconscious adds evidence checks to the research brief
summary: Subconscious argues that a useful brief should specify how an answer will be tested, not just the questions and deliverables. Its template connects the proposed study to a concrete decision.

title: Subconscious examines availability adjustments in conjoint
summary: Adjusting for awareness or distribution changes the interpretation of preference shares. Subconscious explains why those adjustments are different from checking the underlying effects estimated by a choice model.

title: What a cross-tab can tell you about audience differences
summary: Subconscious looks at segment comparisons and the temptation to explain every difference as a cause. Its guide distinguishes describing a pattern from designing a test of why that pattern occurs.

title: Subconscious revisits what open-ended answers can establish
summary: Subconscious explains how to use open-ended questions without treating every stated reason as the cause of a purchase. The piece connects qualitative explanations with follow-up tests of the decision itself.

title: Subconscious distinguishes checking conjoint arithmetic from validation
summary: Subconscious walks through part-worth utilities, the preference scores assigned to product attributes. It explains why reproducing the calculation is a different check from establishing that the preferences reflect the intended buyers.

title: Subconscious sets out its checks for synthetic respondents
summary: Subconscious describes the evidence it wants to see before using a synthetic respondent study. Blind replications and comparisons with human reference data feature in its proposed evaluation process.

title: Electric Twin separates research assistance from audience simulation
summary: A general chatbot can help organize a study without being a model of its participants. Electric Twin examines that distinction and the additional audience context its own approach uses.

title: QualiSynth makes the case for more specific audience definitions
summary: QualiSynth uses a research example to show why a broad label can describe the wrong buyers. Its advice centers on defining who the modeled respondents represent before explaining the study to a client.

title: Simile looks at confidence behind a simulated answer
summary: A single predicted choice leaves out other possible responses. Simile discusses how probability distributions and evaluation can help teams judge how much weight to place on a simulation.

title: Subconscious maps simulation to stages of consulting work
summary: Subconscious describes how research needs change from forming hypotheses to presenting recommendations. It suggests matching simulated studies and further validation to each stage of the engagement.

title: Subconscious applies message testing to recruitment
summary: Subconscious explores comparing employer propositions, job advertisements and careers-page messages. It frames simulated feedback as a way to refine materials before showing them to candidates.

title: Subconscious compares pre-development validation options
summary: The company compares simulation, prototype research with people and experiments before engineering begins. It starts with the assumption most likely to change the product decision.

title: Subconscious compares agencies, synthetic panels and experiments
summary: Subconscious maps three research approaches to different jobs. It looks at the trade-offs between full-service interpretation, fast simulated responses and a study designed around a particular effect.

title: Subconscious separates audience activation from decision testing
summary: Subconscious distinguishes selecting an audience, exploring its possible reactions and testing a controlled choice. The piece explains why these steps answer different marketing questions.

title: Subconscious compares persona chat with managed research
summary: Subconscious considers when a self-service tool or an advisory engagement fits the work. It separates the delivery format from the evidence needed to trust the result.

title: Choosing what a simulated buyer can trade off
summary: Subconscious explains how product attributes and their available levels shape a choice experiment. It focuses on realistic alternatives and avoiding designs that ask participants to compare implausible products.

title: Subconscious connects separate studies into a research roadmap
summary: Subconscious proposes sequencing research so each study informs the next. Its roadmap links exploration, choice testing and later validation instead of treating every brief as a fresh start.

title: Subconscious outlines early concept screening with simulated buyers
summary: The company describes using synthetic consumers to compare rough concepts before commissioning human research. The workflow narrows the candidate set and identifies questions for the next study.

title: Subconscious asks how well models understand real prices
summary: Subconscious examines price grounding in synthetic consumer research. The article argues that fluent explanations of value need to be checked against price-sensitive reference tasks.

title: Subconscious puts the audience and stimulus before the questionnaire
summary: The company recommends fixing the target group, decision and material being tested before drafting questions. It explains how changes in those choices can alter what the eventual answers mean.

title: Subconscious compares the questions pricing methods answer
summary: The company compares willingness-to-pay, price-sensitivity, conjoint and offer-testing approaches. Its guide starts with the pricing decision so teams can choose the method that matches it.

title: Subconscious explores the reasons behind a shifting survey metric
summary: The company proposes testing competing explanations when a tracker moves unexpectedly. Rather than settling on the first plausible story, researchers can design comparisons around the alternatives.

title: Subconscious applies simulation to B2B win-loss questions
summary: Subconscious explores testing possible buying objections before building a sales story around a few interviews. The article focuses on comparing explanations for why business buyers choose or reject an offer.

title: Subconscious examines why a product feature goes unused
summary: Low adoption can reflect poor discovery or confusing naming as well as limited value. Subconscious describes testing those explanations before the next development sprint.

title: Subconscious places simulated ad testing before live experiments
summary: The company describes using simulated buyers to narrow Facebook and LinkedIn ad variants. It then connects that screening step to live tests that measure actual audience behavior.

title: Subconscious brings testable assumptions into client workshops
summary: Subconscious describes structuring a workshop around questions that can be tested. The approach turns disagreements into study options instead of letting the most senior opinion settle the discussion.

title: Subconscious outlines pre-tests for paywall messages
summary: The company describes screening paywall copy with modeled reader groups before using live traffic. The proposed workflow compares segment reactions and then takes selected variants into an actual experiment.

title: Subconscious explores testing welcome emails before sending
summary: Subconscious looks at email order, tone and calls to action through simulated audience reactions. The article positions the exercise as preparation for a real welcome campaign.

title: Subconscious structures B2B marketing questions as experiments
summary: The company describes defining a buying group and varying specific elements of an offer. Its guide emphasizes controlled comparisons rather than asking a model for a broad marketing recommendation.

title: Subconscious explains persona simulation and its evaluation
summary: The company introduces interactive persona simulation and the questions teams can bring to it. It separates the ability to hold a convincing conversation from evidence that the answers fit a research task.

title: Subconscious argues for testing B2B buying roles separately
summary: Subconscious examines the different priorities inside a buying committee. It proposes looking at role-specific objections and trade-offs rather than treating a group discussion as one unified buyer.

title: Articos examines concept testing across countries
summary: Articos argues that translating a questionnaire is only part of a cross-market study. Its guide considers local context and where synthetic screening and human research enter the testing plan.

title: Articos compares participant needs across research methods
summary: Articos reviews how study goals affect recruitment and stopping decisions. It also considers synthetic user research, giving readers a comparison of methods rather than one universal participant count.

title: Articos looks beyond leading questions when tackling bias
summary: Articos examines who designs a study, what the researcher knows and who reviews the findings. The article focuses on structural choices that can shape both human and AI-assisted research.

title: Articos connects concept testing to a go, change or stop decision
summary: The company compares ways to assess whether an idea solves a problem for a defined audience. Its guide focuses on choosing a method for the product's current stage.

title: Articos distinguishes early demand signals from product-market fit
summary: Articos looks at the evidence available before a product has enough users for retention-based analysis. It frames early research as a test of demand assumptions, not proof of established traction.

title: Articos puts buyer evidence before persona decoration
summary: Articos argues that buying triggers and evaluation criteria matter more than a fictional profile's age or photograph. It describes building a usable persona from customer conversations.

title: Articos brings concept, price and messaging into a launch checklist
summary: Articos describes checking the major assumptions behind a launch before committing the budget. It distinguishes that research from simply building a minimum viable product or running a beta.

title: Electric Twin describes how it builds a synthetic audience
summary: The company walks through the move from customer research to an audience model. It describes how source data guides the simulation and how modeled answers are checked against reference responses.

title: Articos examines the questions behind a useful buyer interview
summary: Articos discusses how to ask about buying decisions without steering the answer. The guide covers interview structure, objections and checking whether a script merely confirms the researcher's starting view.

title: Articos reviews where synthetic consumer panels fit
summary: Articos introduces modeled consumer panels and examines their use across different research questions. It discusses why evidence for one task should not automatically be carried over to another.

title: Articos separates simulated patients from synthetic medical records
summary: The company explains two uses of the term synthetic patient: a conversational agent and a generated dataset. Its guide distinguishes research and training uses from decisions about actual patient care.

title: Articos compares AI approaches to ecommerce customer research
summary: Articos examines AI-moderated interviews and synthetic personas as different ways to support ecommerce research. It considers which parts of recruitment, interviewing and analysis each approach changes.

title: Electric Twin outlines a workflow for testing messages
summary: Electric Twin describes comparing messages across modeled customer groups and following up on their reactions. The article covers study setup, interpreting differences and deciding what needs further testing.

title: Articos outlines pre-launch tests for product claims
summary: Articos describes comparing different ways to communicate a product benefit. It distinguishes testing whether wording resonates from establishing that the underlying claim is legally or scientifically supported.

title: Subconscious compares a policy simulation with a published study
summary: Subconscious describes a simulated replication of a published climate-policy study. Its account compares modeled responses with the original research, providing a worked example of its evaluation approach.

title: Articos explores simulated shopper reactions
summary: Articos explains how synthetic shoppers can react to product pages, headlines and price presentations. Its guide focuses on using those responses to refine ideas before testing with customers.

title: Subconscious outlines review rules for AI-assisted research
summary: Subconscious discusses human review and escalation before AI-generated findings enter a client presentation. It recommends setting the rules while designing the workflow, rather than after a disputed output.

title: Subconscious compares simulated and recruited study designs
summary: The company compares research approaches by the decision being made. Its guide explains how an exploratory question can move from simulation into a recruited study with a sharper brief.

title: A browser demo does not establish a model's validity
summary: Subconscious uses browser-based Bayesian modeling to separate software architecture from research quality. Its point: where a model runs does not establish whether the study can answer the decision question.

title: Subconscious separates Bayesian modeling from causal evidence
summary: Subconscious discusses Bayesian approaches to marketing questions, including attribution and customer value. It explains why uncertainty ranges still depend on assumptions and do not automatically establish cause and effect.

title: Articos maps an ecommerce idea from simulation to demand testing
summary: Articos compares concept studies, buyer conversations and behavioral tests before placing a product order. It separates early feedback on an idea from evidence that someone will pay for it.

title: Subconscious proposes questions for inspecting a probability model
summary: Subconscious sets out what a buyer should be able to inspect in a vendor's probability model. The focus is on tracing assumptions through to outputs and understanding what evidence tests those assumptions.

title: Subconscious distinguishes AI analysis from AI-generated participants
summary: Subconscious breaks down what vendors mean by AI-driven research. Its buyer-focused guide separates tools that analyze collected responses from those that generate modeled responses.

title: Keplar separates four meanings of synthetic research
summary: Keplar explains why different research products use the same synthetic label. The piece distinguishes approaches by what they generate and the evidence needed to evaluate their outputs.

title: Stravito shares lessons on scaling AI personas from Quirk's New York
summary: Stravito reports on discussions about deploying AI personas across research and business teams. Its recap focuses on adoption and how organizations put customer knowledge to work.

title: Subconscious considers where agencies can use AI personas
summary: The company examines persona exploration during early client work and the evidence needed for later recommendations. The distinction is between developing a question and supporting a claim.

title: Subconscious tackles the urgent, one-off audience question
summary: Subconscious considers what to check when a team wants a quick simulated answer. It connects the proposed use of that answer to the model's reference data and previous validation tasks.

title: Subconscious asks what comes after the persona document
summary: Subconscious explores turning a static customer profile into a specific research question. The article focuses on testing decisions rather than adding more descriptive details to a persona.

title: Brox examines consent when an interview becomes a digital twin
summary: Brox asks what informed consent means when a model keeps answering new questions after an interview ends. Its perspective revisits privacy, harm and honesty in an ongoing synthetic-research workflow.

title: BluePill launches a marketplace of AI consumer twins
summary: BluePill has launched a marketplace initially focused on US breakfast-food consumers. Brands can choose modeled buyers for chats, surveys, concept tests and packaging studies.

title: Kumkuat launches audience simulation for communications teams
summary: Kumkuat has launched a platform for testing communications with modeled stakeholders, including investors, journalists and policymakers. It is aimed at corporate communications, investor relations and public-affairs teams.

title: Simile announces its Series B
summary: Simile has announced new Series B funding for its work on human-behavior simulation. Its announcement sets out the company's next stage of development and the investors supporting it.

title: Stravito and Lavazza named finalists in the MRS Oppies
summary: Stravito has announced that its work with Lavazza is a finalist in the 2026 MRS Operations Awards. The company's announcement describes the collaboration and the research operations behind it.

title: Articos compares message testing with live A/B tests
summary: Articos breaks down different ways to assess a headline or value proposition. The article looks at what a qualitative response can explain and what a live experiment measures.

title: Electric Twin reports a seven-panel research comparison
summary: Electric Twin describes a preregistered comparison involving seven survey panels and an AI audience, with academic collaborators. Its account explains the study design and the results it uses to assess its model.

title: FishDog questions how synthetic studies are benchmarked
summary: FishDog argues that a human study is itself a measurement with design choices, not a perfect answer key. It discusses what this means when comparing synthetic and recruited research.

title: FishDog examines bias in survey-based comparisons
summary: FishDog reviews different forms of survey bias and their implications for evaluating synthetic research. The article asks readers to examine how a reference study collected its answers before treating those answers as ground truth.

title: Candor proposes six checks for convincing but weak AI answers
summary: Candor examines answers that sound persuasive without offering reliable audience evidence. Its checklist includes looking for suspiciously uniform responses and checking how an answer connects to its source material.

title: Why a generic chatbot is not a customer panel, says Electric Twin
summary: Electric Twin argues that a fluent average answer can hide meaningful audience differences. The article explains its case for grounding models in customer data rather than relying on a persona prompt alone.

title: Electric Twin's CEO examines survey fatigue
summary: Alex Cooper discusses why customers may stop responding to surveys and what that means for research teams. He connects the problem to the company's case for using existing customer evidence in simulations.

title: QualiSynth reports a result that challenged its own hypothesis
summary: In an eight-market synthetic study, QualiSynth tested whether a psychometric layer created differences between markets. The company reports that its preferred explanation did not hold up, while finding effects within personas.

title: Articos sets out checks for an AI-generated persona
summary: Articos examines the inputs used to create synthetic profiles and how teams can evaluate them. Its guide asks what decision the persona will inform before judging whether it is useful.

title: Candor puts audience grounding ahead of model choice
summary: Candor argues that the evidence supplied to a synthetic audience can matter more than the name of the language model. The piece looks at what useful grounding adds to a research conversation.

title: FishDog shares critical feedback from a synthetic game test
summary: FishDog reports what happened when simulated viewers assessed a short game presentation. The example focuses on negative reactions and how the team used them to reconsider the experience.

title: FishDog argues for audience feedback earlier in production
summary: FishDog examines the timing of film and streaming-content testing. Its argument is that simulated screenings can help creative teams explore choices while those choices are still affordable to change.

title: Brox models the friction between wanting to switch and doing it
summary: Brox reports a digital-twin exercise comparing stated shopping intentions with choices made inside specific scenarios. Its account focuses on the practical friction that can keep a modeled customer with an existing provider.

title: FishDog treats scenario planning as rehearsal
summary: FishDog describes using language models to work through possible situations and responses. It distinguishes exploring a scenario from assigning it a reliable probability of happening.

title: Articos considers landing-page research before traffic arrives
summary: Articos explains how to check whether a page makes sense before it has enough visitors for an A/B test. The workflow focuses on specific comprehension questions and open-ended reactions.

title: Brox tests recipe-change recovery messages in a simulated study
summary: Brox presents a Reese's-themed digital-twin exercise involving recipe-change, price and recovery scenarios. The report compares modeled reactions to different responses; it is not a measurement of actual purchases.

title: Candor offers a starting point for team research rules
summary: Candor outlines rules a team can agree before using synthetic research. Its suggested approach covers who reviews outputs, which decisions the work can support and when to bring in real participants.

title: FishDog publishes its view of the synthetic-research landscape
summary: FishDog groups synthetic-research products by the jobs they perform and the ways they model audiences. The guide offers a vendor's perspective on questions buyers can take into product evaluations.

title: FishDog asks buyers to look beyond the model brand
summary: FishDog argues that the surrounding research system matters as much as its underlying language model. It discusses audience construction, study behavior and evaluation as practical buying considerations.

title: FishDog defines its synthetic-population approach
summary: FishDog describes a population platform as more than a collection of isolated persona chats. It explains how persistent agents and group behavior can support different kinds of research questions.

title: QualiSynth compares synthetic interviews with human fieldwork
summary: QualiSynth looks at early exploration and the questions that still need real participants. The article frames synthetic interviews as a way to prepare a study and narrow what researchers take into the field.

title: QualiSynth shows how to rehearse a discussion guide
summary: The company describes using synthetic respondents to try out an interview guide before recruitment. Researchers can inspect confusing questions and weak follow-ups while there is still time to revise the study.

title: Brox shares an interactive surveillance-research walkthrough
summary: Brox demonstrates how digital twins respond to surveillance, privacy and security questions. The walkthrough compares reactions to described products and examines whether familiar brand names change the modeled answers.

title: Stravito proposes a buyer's checklist for AI personas
summary: Stravito outlines questions teams can ask when evaluating an AI persona product. Its guide looks beyond the demo to the research foundation, traceability and practical use of the output.

title: Articos reviews response bias in user research
summary: Articos explains recurring ways the research setting and question design can affect answers. Its guide provides context for teams comparing recruited responses with synthetic research outputs.

title: Candor describes three ways to fit simulation into research
summary: Candor explores workflows that use synthetic research around existing studies. The emphasis is on screening questions and ideas so human research can concentrate on the decisions that need it most.

title: FishDog uses familiar film scenes to examine its screening model
summary: FishDog describes calibrating its synthetic screening tool with well-known film scenes. The account explains the reference material it chose and how it used audience reactions to inspect the model.

title: Panoplai's Adam Bai discusses the changing insights workflow
summary: Panoplai shares Adam Bai's appearance on the Greenbook podcast. The conversation covers the company's approach to research and how AI is changing the work of insights teams.

title: Brox simulates insurance renewal and switching decisions
summary: Brox compares renewal scenarios and alternative letters with a synthetic customer panel. The exercise explores price changes, competing offers and claims experiences as possible influences on modeled retention.

title: Yabble uses Virtual Audiences to explore competitors
summary: Yabble demonstrates competitor questions through an Australian streaming example. The article shows how teams can use Virtual Audiences to explore alternatives and the reasons behind modeled preferences.

title: Electric Twin introduces the building blocks of synthetic audiences
summary: This introduction explains what a modeled audience is and how teams can question it. Electric Twin uses product and communication decisions to illustrate the workflow.
